results.rationale: Section 4-7B(a) explicitly requires prescribed plants and plant products prepared at a registered establishment to be traced from the property (if any) from which they were transferred to the registered establishment.
Section 4-7B(b) explicitly requires traceability while the plants or plant products are at the registered establishment.
Section 4-7B(c) explicitly requires traceability to the premises to which they are transferred from the registered establishment.

Section 4-3(3) requires a system of controls to ensure compliance with conditions including traceability (section 4-7B) and integrity (section 4-8). These sections collectively govern the obligation for systems of controls to maintain traceability and integrity.

No section explicitly requires a product flow chart; however, the traceability requirement in section 4-7B, the system of controls in section 4-3(3), and the definition of flowpath in section 1-6 provide the closest governing basis for demonstrating movement and integrity.

Section 4-3(3) requires a system of controls to ensure compliance with conditions; section 4-9(3) prohibits blending of failed goods; section 9-11 governs reassessment and treatment after failed assessment; section 4-8A sets treatment conditions. Together they govern the system of controls for managing failed goods.

Section 4-7A(2)(b) requires pests and contaminants to be controlled appropriately; section 4-2(4)(c) requires design and construction to minimise infestation or contamination. These govern the obligation to maintain phytosanitary security against contamination/infestation.
Section 4-8 requires integrity to be ensured, and section 4-7B requires traceability; together they address minimising substitution risk, though no section explicitly mentions 'substitution'.

Section 4-11 prescribes detailed packaging requirements for prescribed plants or plant products at registered establishments, including cleaning, appropriateness, integrity, strength, and importing country requirements.

Section 11-7 requires the occupier to retain documents relevant to compliance (including traceability under section 4-7B) for at least 2 years; section 11-2 specifies record format requirements (English, dated, accurate, legible, auditable).

Section 11-7 requires retention of all documents relevant to compliance for 2 years, which includes records of rejected/failed goods, blending, treatments, and re-presentation; section 11-2 specifies record format.
Section 11-2(1) directly states that records must be in English, dated, accurate, legible, and able to be audited.
Section 4-7 explicitly states that all importing country requirements relating to export operations carried out at a registered establishment must be met.
